samples.summary: Cleanup write is a second Yorkie undo unit, so Cmd+Z after a block-type change / style redefinition undoes only the invisible cleanup
samples.evidence: `Doc.setBlockType` now does `this.store.setBlockType(...)` (one `doc.update()` in YorkieDocStore, line 1415) followed by `this.dropStaleStyleOff(blockId)` → `store.applyStyles(...)` which opens a *second* `doc.update()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1806). YorkieDocStore.snapshot() is a documented no-op ("Yorkie tracks undo units via doc.update()", line 2727-2728), so undo granularity is per-update. The same applies to `afterNamedStyleChange()` in view/editor.ts:1052 — `writeStylesAndRematerialize` explicitly bundles itself into "a single `doc.update` so the whole change is one undo unit" (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2681), and `dropStaleStyleOffAll()` adds another update after it. Result: whenever anything stale is found (exactly the interesting case), the first Cmd+Z restores dead `false` flags — a change with no visual effect — and the user must press undo twice to revert the block-type change or the style reset. The code comments in document.ts:492-493 and editor.ts:1049-1050 assert the opposite ("stays one undo unit", "undo as one step"), which holds only for MemDocStore's snapshot-based history.

samples.summary: Internal-clipboard table-cell paste bypasses the new dropStaleStyleOffAll cleanup
samples.evidence: The block branch of the internal-clipboard paste calls `this.doc.dropStaleStyleOffAll()` (text-editor.ts:1264) with the rationale that the internal clipboard is the only payload preserving an explicit `italic: false`. The sibling branch at line 1247-1253 (`data.tableCells` → `this.pasteTableCells(...)`) carries blocks from the *same* internal clipboard payload and never runs the cleanup, so a run copied out of a Heading 6 cell into a plain cell keeps exactly the dead flag #749 is about.
searchedFor: grep applyStyle/applyInlineStyle call sites in packages/docs/src

samples.summary: captureFormatAtCursor ignores the hyperlink underline default, so the painter copies underline:false from a source run that renders underlined
samples.evidence: `on()` computes `raw[key] ?? defaults[key]` where `defaults` is only the named-style layer (`styleDefaultsAtCursor`). `renderRun` (view/paint-layout.ts:398-401) treats an absent `underline` on an `href` run as underlined — the second default layer this very change documents. Copying format from a link therefore yields `underline: false`, and the result differs by target: on a target that is already a link `styleOffAsClear`'s `rangeCarriesLink` keeps the `false` (link paints un-underlined, unlike the source), while on a plain target the key is cleared and, if the buffer also carries `href` (it spreads `raw`), the pasted link comes out underlined. The doc comment claims the value read is "the *effective* one".

samples.summary: Structural inlines can no longer re-merge after a boundary split, so a split page-number/image run stays duplicated
samples.evidence: `normalizeInlines` now refuses to merge any pair where either side is structural (`isStructuralInline`), regardless of equality. Previously a structural run split at a style-range boundary (applyInlineStyle pushes head/tail slices with identical styles) was re-merged on the next normalize; now the two halves persist as two runs each carrying `style.pageNumber`/`style.image`, which renderers substitute/paint per run — i.e. the field or image is rendered twice while the text offsets count the original characters. Only reachable when a structural run's text is longer than one character (e.g. text inserted into a pageNumber run), so the risk is small, but the exception has no length guard.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. Doc.setBlockType (document.ts:606-611) performs store.setBlockType followed by dropStaleStyleOff -> writeStaleStyleOffEdits -> store.applyStyles (document.ts:566). In YorkieDocStore these are two separate transactions: setBlockType opens doc.update at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1461 and applyStyles opens its own doc.update at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1806. Undo granularity in that store is strictly per doc.update — snapshot() is an explicit no-op (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2727-2729) and undo() calls doc.history.undo() once (2731-2736); undoFloor (558/573/776) only limits depth and does not group. The editor's undoFn (editor.ts:1995-2020) invokes docStore.undo() once per Cmd+Z with no skip/loop for no-op units. The same pattern applies to the named-style path: writeStylesAndRematerialize is one doc.update (2686-2716) and afterNamedStyleChange (editor.ts:1052-1056) adds dropStaleStyleOffAll's applyStyles as a second update. So whenever stale false flags exist, the first undo reverts only the invisible cleanup and a second undo is needed — contradicting the in-code invariants stated at document.ts:492-493 and editor.ts:1049-1050, which only hold for MemDocStore's snapshot-based history (memory.ts:159). The path is production-reachable (docs-view.tsx:322 constructs YorkieDocStore). No guard makes it unreachable; it is a real broken invariant / incorrect user-visible behavior in the correctness lane.
